title: Disprove the universal Omega cut and prove the dyadic error asymptotic (no κ)
body:
At 128 factors, a later scratch readout has formal accumulated error mass 26,144 versus 26,028 at Omega, refuting #2177 C1. An exact family beats Omega at every dyadic size from 128 onward. The written proof also gives E_inf(2^h) <= 2*4^h-3^h and E_inf(2^h)/4^h -> 2.

#2735's fixed-cut theorem remains intact. #6668/#6770 address single-channel or interval transport; this result concerns the total across independent completed-leaf errors. It does not claim an exact finite-size maximizer or a universal error-budget profile.

Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a.
Source heads: #2177 2cbbb48d3b580e018312278c97b63817de963be7; #2735 90a507b39063cfaebdf92794fcb9d18f358439a6. Five live inputs have Git-blob/SHA256 pins in SOURCES.json.

Reproduce:
`python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-omega-counterexample`
Expected: PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE, outcome=completed.

Executed: 134 source-order comparisons; 32 literal profiles; 28 generalized-family replays; 4,950 integer recurrence checks; separate forward replay of all 16,384 leaves matching both complete signed channel digests; 1,954 paired-prefix checks. All 14 semantic controls and six actual source/receipt corruption controls passed. Both engines passed cold Git-free optimized Python replay. Commit bytes/modes, export input coverage, remote branch/parent and complete tree equality were checked.

No new κ. Formal free-algebra, completed-leaf model only: native rounding, internal leaf errors, exact finite maxima and selected-caller integration remain open. All five selected assumptions remain. No proof-kernel, independent human review or full-history ancestry audit is claimed.

Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Credit #628 (Chafik Boukhalfa), #2067 (Adam Gall), #2177 (Philippe Van Velzen), #2735 (ywz65), and retained predecessors.

[Published proof, witness, checks and full handoff](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/c134aa6edc8ed6444bbf7bfcabbed8124ff26c39/research/dyadic-omega-counterexample)
